name: Solitary Cell
narrativeOnEnter: A tiny room, barely two metres across. The walls are padded — old foam, mouldering now — and the single overhead light is caged behind thick wire mesh. There is no window. There is no furniture. There is only the drain in the floor and a hook on the ceiling.

action.text:
The foam padding is rotting, pulling away from the wall in strips. Behind it: bare concrete — and words. Layers of them, written at different heights, over what must have been months.

First layer (near the floor, scratched with something small):
'4031'
'I KNOW WHAT THEY'RE DOING TO US'
'THE SESSIONS ARE NOT THERAPY'
'MY NAME IS ELARA VOSS AND I WAS A NEUROSCIENTIST'
'I PUBLISHED PAPERS ON CONSENT IN COGNITIVE RESEARCH'
'THE IRONY IS NOT LOST ON ME'

Second layer (middle of the wall, written faster, more ragged):
'47 OF US. MAPPED. ARCHIVED. SOLD.
WHAT WILL THEY BUILD FROM OUR MINDS?
WHAT DID WE BECOME WITHOUT KNOWING?

IF YOU FIND THIS: WE WERE PEOPLE.
WE WERE NOT DATA.
AXIOM TOOK SOMETHING FROM EACH OF US
THAT WE CANNOT GET BACK.
BUT YOU CAN MAKE SURE THEY PAY FOR IT.
TELL SOMEONE. TELL EVERYONE.'

Third layer (high up, calmer, deliberate):
'Harlan told me about the tunnel tonight.
I'm leaving tomorrow.
I'm taking my list.
Someday, AXIOM will have to answer for all 47 names on it.

I will be there when they do.
— E. Voss'

And below everything, a different hand entirely. Shakier. Later:

'She was right. She escaped.
I stayed. I'm too old to run.
I'm writing this so someone knows she was here.
She was real. She was brave.
She told the truth in this room for eight months
before anyone listened.
— M. Farrow, Patient 11'
A rusted metal drain in the centre of the floor. Nothing more. You don't want to think about why it's there.
An iron hook, bolted into the ceiling. No context provided. No context needed.
